From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Performance SLO benchmark methodology  follow-up

Sam / Priya,

Thanks again for a productive call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a shared baseline for the benchmark run: 

Summary of targets you mentioned:
- Latency: 95th percentile <= 250ms for short-form generation (<=512 tokens).
- Streaming: time-to-first-token < 500ms; steady-state per-token gap <= 40ms.
- Throughput: sustained 50 req/s for the primary endpoint (mixed prompt mix).
- Concurrency: expected peak concurrent in-production = 20 workers; we'd like to test up to 40 to validate headroom.

Benchmark items Redwood needs from EdgeFin:
1) Prompt set (representative mix: short queries, long completion, instruction-following)  ideally CSV with columns: id, prompt, expected_token_count, category.
2) Eval harness (scripts or docker image) to reproduce request pacing, concurrency profile, and streaming behavior.
3) Measurement definitions you prefer for pass/fail (e.g., 95th latency, cold-start vs warm, allowable error rate).
4) Target windows (steady-state duration, any warmup/caching behavior).

Proposed Redwood measurement definitions (we can align):
- Warmup: 120s with progressive ramp to target QPS.
- Steady-state sampling window: 10 minutes at target QPS.
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency (request completed), time-to-first-token (TTFT), tokens/sec, throughput achieved, error rate, and cost estimate per 1M tokens.
- Streaming: measure time-to-first-byte (TTFB), TTFT, and inter-token gap distribution.

If that looks good, please share the prompt set + eval harness (or a Drive link) and we can schedule an initial baseline run from a Redwood dedicated test cluster. Suggested date window: May 2628 (your timezone).

Next steps:
- EdgeFin: share prompt_set.csv and evaluation harness (or link)
- Redwood: produce a reproducible benchmark runbook and initial baseline report within 48 hours of the run

Thanks cc'ing Rishi and Vivek to coordinate harness details and infra.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Performance SLO benchmark methodology  follow-up

Thanks Marissa md great summary. Confirming the targets are accurate for our core route. We pulled together an initial prompt set and a lightweight harness we use internally. I attached the files to this email: prompt_set_v2.csv (includes metadata columns) and eval_harness_v1.zip (python harness + README).

A few notes on our side:
- The prompt set includes a ~60/30/10 split: short Q/A, long summarization, and instruction/chain-of-thought-style prompts.
- For streaming, we use chunked HTTP with SSE for progress tokens. Time-to-first-token is critical for UX md we prioritize first token latency over throughput in interactive flows.
- Hardware we expect in prod is A100 80GB (nvlink), but we can provide a secondary spec (4x A10) for cost comparison.

We can make the Drive folder available here: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/edgefin-benchmarks (permissions set to Redwood view).

Proposed run: May 27 in the morning PST. If Redwood can run from a similar GPU SKU (A100) that would be ideal for apples-to-apples.

Attaching: prompt_set_v2.csv, eval_harness_v1.zip

mdSam

Thanks Sam md that helps. A few additions from the bench/harness side to make results reproducible and actionable on our end: 

Measurement and reproducibility checklist:
- Pin model artifact (model name + sha or S3 path) and quantization flags (if any).
- Hardware: specify instance type, CUDA/cuDNN versions, and driver version. If you can share an AMI/Dockerfile that helps.
- Warmup: we recommend 300s for models with KV cache priming in long-context workloads. Clearly separate cold-start runs (no warmed weights/kv) vs warmed runs.
- Network conditions: please indicate expected inter-region latency; we'll simulate 10ms/50ms/100ms to check sensitivity.
- Streaming metrics: record TTFB, TTFT, first N-token latencies (N=1,4,8), and inter-token gap percentiles.
- Concurrency/throughput validation: run steps at concurrency = {1,5,10,20,40} and report achieved QPS and error ratios.

Operational notes:
- We'll run the harness in a reproducible container. If EdgeFin can add a small wrapper script that pins seed and returns deterministic prompt IDs, that will help mapping errors back to prompts.
- For cost estimates, include your instance spot vs reserved pricing expectations.

If everyone is aligned, Marissa: Redwood will plan a baseline run on May 27 (09001200 PST) using A100-equivalent infra and share the detailed report + raw traces (sample_trace.json) by EOD May 28.

Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
